```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2023_crime_waste.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Build W matrix
boroughs = sorted(df['borough'].unique())
n = len(boroughs)
borough_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

W_binary = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W_binary[i, j] = 1

W = np.zeros_like(W_binary)
for i in range(n):
    row_sum = W_binary[i].sum()
    W[i] = W_binary[i] / row_sum

# Get values
crime = df.set_index('borough').loc[boroughs, 'Crime_value'].values
waste = df.set_index('borough').loc[boroughs, 'Waste_value'].values

# Standardize
z_crime = (crime - crime.mean()) / crime.std(ddof=1)
z_waste = (waste - waste.mean()) / waste.std(ddof=1)

# Compute Lee's L
numerator = z_crime @ (W @ z_waste)
term_x = z_crime @ (W @ z_crime)
term_y = z_waste @ (W @ z_waste)
L_obs = numerator / np.sqrt(term_x * term_y)

print('Numerator:', numerator)
print('term_x (spatial variance of Crime):', term_x)
print('term_y (spatial variance of Waste):', term_y)
print('Lee\'s L observed:', L_obs)

# Permutation test
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 999
L_perm = np.empty(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    perm = np.random.permutation(n)
    z_waste_p = z_waste[perm]
    num_p = z_crime @ (W @ z_waste_p)
    term_y_p = z_waste_p @ (W @ z_waste_p)
    # Note: term_x doesn't change, only term_y might change under permutation
    # Actually, term_y_p is the same as term_y because we're just permuting labels
    # but the spatial weights structure is fixed. However, since W is row-standardized
    # and symmetric? Wait, is W symmetric?
    # Actually term_y_p = z_waste_p' W z_waste_p. This is NOT necessarily equal to term_y
    # because the permutation changes which values are neighbors of which.
    L_perm[i] = num_p / np.sqrt(term_x * term_y_p)

# Two-tailed p-value
abs_L_obs = abs(L_obs)
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(L_perm) >= abs_L_obs) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
print('Permutation p-value (two-tailed):', p_value)
print('Mean of null distribution:', np.mean(L_perm))
print('Std of null distribution:', np.std(L_perm))
print('Min/max of null:', np.min(L_perm), np.max(L_perm))
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2023_crime_waste.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop boroughs with missing data
df_clean = df.dropna()
valid_boroughs = sorted(df_clean['borough'].unique())
n = len(valid_boroughs)
print('Valid boroughs after dropping NaNs:', n)
print('Dropped boroughs:', sorted(set(df['borough'].unique()) - set(valid_boroughs)))

# Build row-standardized spatial weights matrix for valid boroughs
borough_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(valid_boroughs)}
W_binary = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)
valid_set = set(valid_boroughs)
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b, ne = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    if b in valid_set and ne in valid_set:
        W_binary[borough_idx[b], borough_idx[ne]] = 1.0

W = np.zeros_like(W_binary)
for i in range(n):
    row_sum = W_binary[i].sum()
    W[i] = W_binary[i] / row_sum

print('Any zero row sums?', (W.sum(axis=1) == 0).any())
print('W is symmetric?', np.allclose(W, W.T))

# Extract and standardize variables
crime = df_clean.set_index('borough').loc[valid_boroughs, 'Crime_value'].values
waste = df_clean.set_index('borough').loc[valid_boroughs, 'Waste_value'].values

z_crime = (crime - crime.mean()) / crime.std(ddof=0)
z_waste = (waste - waste.mean()) / waste.std(ddof=0)

# Compute Lee's L
num_obs = z_crime @ (W @ z_waste)
term_x = z_crime @ (W @ z_crime)
term_y = z_waste @ (W @ z_waste)
L_obs = num_obs / np.sqrt(term_x * term_y)

print('Observed Lee\'s L:', L_obs)
print('Numerator:', num_obs)
print('term_x:', term_x)
print('term_y:', term_y)

# Permutation test with 999 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 999
L_perm = np.empty(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    perm = np.random.permutation(n)
    z_waste_p = z_waste[perm]
    num_p = z_crime @ (W @ z_waste_p)
    term_y_p = z_waste_p @ (W @ z_waste_p)
    L_perm[i] = num_p / np.sqrt(term_x * term_y_p)

# Two-sided p-value
abs_L = abs(L_obs)
extreme = np.sum(np.abs(L_perm) >= abs_L)
p_value = (extreme + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

print('Mean null L:', np.mean(L_perm))
print('Std null L:', np.std(L_perm))
print('Extreme count:', extreme)
print('Two-tailed p-value:', p_value)
```
